clue.text: As one who's often scored, ex-Chelsea star's dropped a line about period of sexual activity

indicators.note: the trimmed footballer's name sits about, i.e. around, the mating-season word
the footballer's name has had something dropped from it, so letters are taken away

parts.note: John Terry, long-serving former captain of Chelsea football club
RY, short for railway, is a standard crossword 'line'
the rut is the mating season of deer and similar animals

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style tale of a retired Chelsea footballer losing a line during a randy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' leaves JOHNTER and 'about' puts RUT within it. The definition is a pun: a composer is 'scored' because he writes scores, not because he is cut or seduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolific composer writes musical scores, so he is often associated with scoring in the musical sense.

clue.text: Selfishness shown by online reordering of 20D

parts.note: E- is the prefix for electronic or online things, as in e-mail

indicators.note: reordering asks for the letters of the 20 down answer to be put in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 20 down, a word for a gadget

explanation.surface: Someone's self-absorption shows in how they keep rearranging their gadget online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reordering of' scrambles the 20 down answer; the e- of online things supplies the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting oneself first is the core of a self-centred outlook, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: "Odd choice of choirs", said chap in outlying region of France

indicators.note: choosing the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on, of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man remarks that a choir he heard was an odd choice, somewhere remote in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Odd choice of choirs' look like a remark; in fact 'Odd choice of' picks letters 1, 3, 5... from CHOIRS SAID CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island is a French region lying well away from the mainland, hence outlying.

clue.text: This is the day to rest choir's 6, tenor having gone to spa

definitions.text: This is the day to rest

indicators.note: the remaining letters go to, i.e. are joined onto, the spa town
the tenor having gone means that voice-part letter is removed

parts.note: 6 across is SINGERS; a choir's singers are soprano, alto, tenor and bass, abbreviated SATB on scores
T is the standard abbreviation for tenor on choral music
Bath is the famous spa city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: A choir rests on its day off, with the tenor slipping away to a spa.
explanation.walkthrough: Choral scores label the four voice parts by initials, soprano, alto, tenor, bass; 'having gone' removes the tenor's, and 'to' attaches the spa city.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekly day of rest in Jewish and Christian tradition is a holy day when work stops.

clue.text: 16D girl? Possibly 16A, taking English for a gas

definitions.note: 16 down is COLLEGE; the clue wants a word that is both a Cambridge college and a girl's name

indicators.note: possibly signals the swapped letters may be arranged in another way
taking one letter in exchange for another, so one letter replaces another
for here means in place of: the English letter stands in place of the gas

parts.note: the answer to 16 across, a festive song
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, a gas

explanation.surface: A girl at college might sing a carol, swapping a gas for English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking English for a gas' turns CAROL into CAREL; 'Possibly' rearranges that. The question mark flags that a girl's name is only one example of what the word is.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of a Cambridge college and also a common female first name.

clue.text: Wrong football team has managed to lose? Rats!

definitions.note: rats are informers, people who squeal to the police; plural like the answer

parts.note: a wrong or misdeed is a sin

indicators.note: the team name is made to lose the letters for 'managed'

parts.note: Rangers, the Glasgow football club
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A fan curses as the wrong football team has managed to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats!' reads as an exclamation of annoyance but is the noun: informers who 'sing' to the police. Rangers is a Glasgow football club; 'to lose' strips the word for managed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informers are said to sing when they tell the police everything, so rats and the answer are slang synonyms.

clue.text: Put on list for jury service, Hob's getting off plane

definitions.text: Put on list for jury service

parts.note: Hob is the setter, so 'Hob's' is 'I am', shortened to I'M

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter, called for jury duty, is getting off a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often refers to himself by name, so 'Hob's' is I'M. 'getting off' scrambles PLANE into PANEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol someone on a jury panel is to list them for jury duty; it is a legal verb.

clue.text: Piece of music from 1 (a 20A)

indicators.note: from says the letters come out of the run of words that follows, hidden inside it, with the rest discarded

parts.note: the answer to 1 down, the composer's name
the answer to 20 across, a song title

explanation.surface: A piece of music by the composer, one of his settings of a Gloria.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the cross-references as words: JOHN RUTTER A GLORIA, and the answer is hidden across the end of RUTTER, A and the start of GLORIA, so everything around it is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragtime tune, as by Scott Joplin, is a kind of syncopated piano piece.

clue.text: Bass about soprano: "Flipping stuck-up sort"

indicators.note: flipping turns the string of letters over so it reads backwards

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for bass on choral music
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A bass complains about a soprano: 'Flipping stuck-up sort'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse but turns BONS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who looks down on those of lower status is a stuck-up type, a synonym.

clue.text: Being resigned to doing without a mushroom

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for doing goes outside the mushroom

parts.note: acting is doing, as in taking action
the cep or porcini is an edible mushroom

explanation.surface: Someone accepts having to go without a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but here has its old sense, outside: the word for doing goes outside the mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a situation without resisting is the same as being resigned to it.

clue.text: River crossing 5 16D's city

definitions.note: 5 down and 16 down together name a college whose city is wanted

parts.note: the Cam flows through the English university city it names
a bridge is a crossing over a river

explanation.surface: A river crossing in the city of a well-known college.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare College is one of the colleges of the university in this English city.

clue.text: Kind of anthem: timelessly fresh and intrinsically universal

indicators.note: intrinsically means inside, so the universal letter goes within
fresh signals the remaining letters are made new, rearranged
time-less: the letter for time, T, is dropped from the word for the hymn

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A sort of anthem praised as timeless, fresh and universal at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like 'type of', but 'Kind' is the adjective. 'timelessly' drops T from ANTHEM, 'fresh' rearranges ANHEM to HMANE, and 'intrinsically' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing compassion and gentleness toward others makes one kind, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Lowest note? Second in sung Mass

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half-note

indicators.note: the second letter in the following word is taken

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A singer asks for the lowest note held for a second in a sung Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowest note?' reads as one phrase, but 'note' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The least possible amount or level is the smallest, the bottom of the range.

clue.text: Hymn needing organ briefly? Arranged without one, in fact

indicators.note: briefly means the word for the periodical is cut short to its familiar clipped form

parts.note: an organ is a periodical, a magazine, the mouthpiece of a party or group

indicators.note: arranged means the pooled letters are set in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hymn needs a short organ arrangement, played without one person, in fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' is not the instrument but a periodical, and 'briefly' clips it. 'Arranged' rearranges the letters of IN FACT together with the one, giving NIFICAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Song of Mary from Luke's gospel is a canticle sung at Evensong and Vespers.

clue.text: Edit choral piece that's really long?

definitions.note: to long for something badly, a verb phrase

indicators.note: a piece is a part of the words that follow, hidden inside them

explanation.surface: Someone asks to edit a choral piece that is too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective about the piece; it is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a strong restless desire for something is to yearn intensely for it.

clue.text: Happily sing choral composition that's not hard

indicators.note: composition means the remaining letters are composed into a new order
the word becomes one that's not got the hard letter, so it is removed

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A cheerful singer chooses a choral composition that isn't difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not hard' drops H from CHORAL, then 'composition' rearranges CORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to sing joyfully, as of birds or festive singers.

clue.text: Old King's lecturer, say, resident in it?

definitions.text: Old King's lecturer, say, resident in it?

indicators.note: resident in means living inside, so these letters go within the king's name

parts.note: Old King Cole, the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme
say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A question about a lecturer at King's, perhaps one who lives there.
explanation.walkthrough: King's is itself a Cambridge college and its lecturers may live in, so the whole clue describes the answer while the wordplay puts L and EG in COLE.
explanation.definitionFit: King's at Cambridge is an academic institution where a lecturer might also reside.

clue.text: Choir's foremost mature composer

indicators.note: foremost means the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: to age is to mature

explanation.surface: The choir's leading figure is a mature composer.
explanation.walkthrough: John Cage was the American avant-garde composer of 4'33''.
explanation.definitionFit: The American experimentalist wrote music, famously the silent piece, so he is an example.

clue.text: Rearranged 16A? He gets a complaint

indicators.note: rearranged means the letters pooled together are put into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 16 across, a festive song
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man reworking a carol gets told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance but is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an illness, and this is a serious bacterial intestinal disease.

clue.text: Unnerved conductor with loud ending

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle, the British conductor

indicators.note: ending means the final letter of the word next to it

explanation.surface: A conductor is thrown when a piece ends loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Simon Rattle led the Berlin Philharmonic and the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shaken or made nervous is to be flustered, so the past participles match.

clue.text: Muted trombone's finale, playing hymn

indicators.note: playing means the letters are moved about, rearranged
the finale is the end, so the last letter of the instrument's name

explanation.surface: A muted trombone finishes playing a hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges MUTED plus E, the last of TROMBONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin canticle of praise opening 'We praise thee, O God' is sung at services.

clue.text: Ring a girl about Van Morrison song

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the pooled letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a girl about a Van Morrison song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges O with the letters of A GIRL. The song was a 1964 hit for Them, Van Morrison's band.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the famous 1964 rock single written by Van Morrison, spelling out a girl's name.

clue.text: Gadget item somehow messing with our heads?

definitions.text: Gadget item somehow messing with our heads?

indicators.note: heads are the first letters of the words in the clue

explanation.surface: A gadget that messes with our minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes the first letter of each word from the start of the clue through 'our', skipping the link 'with'; the whole clue describes a mind-bending device.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a contraption or device whose name one cannot recall.

clue.text: Essentially free thinkers, those like Christ

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so the middle letters of the word are taken

parts.note: deemers are those who deem, i.e. think or judge

explanation.surface: Free thinkers likened to Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes RE from the heart of FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ is called the Redeemer, one who saves people from sin, so such saviours are like him.

clue.text: Fishballs?

parts.note: eggs of a fish, and the soft milt or testes of a male fish, are both called by this word

explanation.surface: Fishballs, as a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Fishballs suggests a food; the joke is that 'balls' also means testes, and soft milt is called by the same word as hard fish eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg mass of a female fish and the milt of a male fish share this name.

clue.text: Fine piece from 1 I clued

definitions.note: a blood-money fine in old Irish law, a noun

indicators.note: a piece from means some letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the answer to 1 down, the composer's name

explanation.surface: A fine bit from the composer, as the setter clued it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 1 as JOHN RUTTER; the answer spans the end of RUTTER and I CLUED. 'Fine' is not the adjective but the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Irish law this was the compensation paid by a killer to the victim's family, a blood-fine.

clue.text: Piece of music by rock band, with short piano introduction

indicators.note: the shortened word is introduced into the band name, put inside it

parts.note: R.E.M. is the American rock band

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off at its final letter

parts.note: piano in music means soft or quiet

explanation.surface: A song by a rock band, with a brief piano opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' is not the instrument but the musical marking for soft; 'short' cuts its last letter, and 'introduction' puts what remains inside the band's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mass for the dead and its musical settings, as by Mozart or Fauré, is a kind of composition.

clue.text: Escaped from one-time capital in Germany after vacation

indicators.note: in places the trimmed Canadian city within the emptied country name
after vacation the word is emptied, leaving only its outer letters
one time less: one of the letters for time, T, is taken away

parts.note: Ottawa is the capital of Canada

explanation.surface: Someone escaped from a former German capital after a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-time capital' looks like a former capital such as Bonn, but 'one-time' removes one T from Canada's capital. 'after vacation' empties Germany to its outer letters, and 'in' puts the trimmed city inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fled or got clear of capture is the same as having escaped.
